A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Meta-RFFT research despite the changed title and organization. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Qwen-7B and Qwen-32B fine-tuning and one-shot experiments, error analyses, and training ablations in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds evaluations of long-CoT models, PPO training, Tulu3, and pretraining task diversity in Sections 4-5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Meta-RFFT retains supervised multi-task rule-following pretraining followed by target-task fine-tuning or one-shot adaptation. Rule recitation, variable-state traces, and synthetic augmentation from 22 snippets are retained. PPO is introduced as a comparison method, not a component of Meta-RFFT.

E1.justification: Table 1 revises reported BBH coverage from eight tasks to six, reducing total/pretraining task counts from 88/76 to 86/74. The four domains and twelve downstream tasks remain. V1 does not identify the two formerly counted tasks; v2's full task catalogue primarily adds documentation.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained direct-answer, scratchpad, and vanilla-RFFT baselines, v2 evaluates DeepSeek-R1-671B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-7B, QwQ-32B, PPO-trained Qwen-7B, and Tulu3. It also introduces a single-task RF-pretraining control. These are reported comparisons in Tables 2-3 and Figures 7, 10-11, and 17.

E3.justification: V2 adds ACC_Len30 and Max_Len_90% aggregate metrics, long-CoT testing with temperature zero and a 24,000-token cap, PPO training, and a Llama-3.1-8B comparison. That comparison uses target fine-tuning for Meta-RFFT versus one-shot Tulu3 prompting. The original lengths 1-5 training, lengths 6-30 testing, and 100 examples per test length remain.

E4.justification: V2 adds a one-versus-74 pretraining-task ablation, an outcome-reward PPO comparison, and worked DeepSeek-R1 and PPO failure cases (Figure 17, Figure 7, and Tables 8-9). These examine task diversity and failures of rule adherence. Existing loop-count, natural-language-rule, training-curve, and data-size analyses are retained, including material moved into Appendix E.

E5.justification: V1 Figure 3 explicitly identifies error bars as 95% confidence intervals; v2 Figure 4 drops that explanation while retaining error bars. The same three-seed training curves remain in v1 Figure 10 and v2 Figure 14. No increase in repeated runs or new statistical procedure is established.

E6.justification: V2 adds long-CoT, PPO, Tulu3, task-diversity, and four-task NUPA one-shot results, together with aggregate scores in Tables 2-3. Existing results also change: 7B vanilla RFFT on LC Move Zeroes at length six rises from approximately 51% to 97% in v1 Figure 2 versus v2 Figure 3. The original 32B fine-tuning curves are retained.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix D.3 adds explicit mathematical definitions of the PPO policy objective and value loss in Equations 1-2, absent from v1. This is a limited formal addition for the new comparator; no theorem, proof, or theoretical guarantee for Meta-RFFT is introduced.

C1.justification: V2 refocuses the abstract and conclusion on robust cross-task length generalization, adds a first-framework novelty claim, and prominently claims superiority over leading long-CoT models. Its abstract highlights 95% accuracy on 30-digit addition versus 72% for DeepSeek-R1-671B and 32% for QwQ-32B. V1 primarily claims transferable rule-following improvements over its original baselines.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations about outcome-reward RL encouraging direct-answer shortcuts, the necessity of diverse pretraining tasks, and amortized computational efficiency. Appendix A explicitly limits applicability to controlled tasks and identifies unresolved legal/workflow applications and length definitions. V1's discussion of cheaper direct-answer or scratchpad approaches sometimes outperforming vanilla RFFT is removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds annotator training, qualification, and validation procedures; a catalogue of all 86 tasks with splits and length definitions; H800 hardware and training-time breakdowns; and PPO hyperparameters (Appendices C.1, D.2-D.3, and H). The original core training hyperparameters remain in Table 5, previously Table 3.

R1.justification: V2 adds substantial positioning against instruction-following approaches, citing Tulu3, Alpaca, WizardLM, and Super-NaturalInstructions, and develops comparisons with long-CoT reasoning and outcome-supervised RL. It removes the expert-versus-novice cognitive analogy and associated references. This changes the research framing beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and results narrative are extensively rewritten. V2 creates a standalone Analysis section, consolidates data-size discussion in the appendix, relocates the impact statement, and reorganizes the appendices with a contents page. These are substantial language and structural revisions.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. V2 separates and redraws the overview diagrams, rearranges error-analysis panels, changes plot colors and legends, and expands one-shot grids from eight to twelve tasks. It adds comparison plots, aggregate and compute tables, error-case tables, and a multipage task catalogue.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves important documentation gaps through the complete task catalogue, annotation procedures, and compute disclosures. New long-CoT comparisons and the task-diversity control test important alternatives left unexamined in v1, while explicit limitations better bound applicability. These substantially improve assessability and reproducibility. The unequal Tulu adaptation settings and broad interpretation of the limited PPO experiment weaken some new conclusions, and the confidence-interval explanation is lost, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the gains.
